explanation: The `case 'gold':` branch is missing a `break` statement, so execution falls through into `case 'silver':` and overwrites `discount` with 0.1 before hitting the break there. As a result, a 'gold' tier customer silently receives the silver discount (0.1) instead of the intended 0.2 — every other case works correctly because they all have their own `break`.
prompt: Does this discount switch statement work correctly for every tier?
snippet:
function getDiscount(tier) {
  let discount = 0
  switch (tier) {
    case 'gold':
      discount = 0.2
    case 'silver':
      discount = 0.1
      break
    case 'bronze':
      discount = 0.05
      break
    default:
      discount = 0
  }
  return discount
}
